thread:
support-ingress: FYI customer Globex reported sudden p99 jumps across EU clusters after last night's infra updates. multiple tracebacks showing backend stalls, customer is seeing timeout errors and high ttfb. linking logs shortly.
eng-runtime: can you paste the request ids and example timestamps? are these from hosted API or Dedicated pools?
support-ingress: hosted API (eu-west-2). sample reqs: req=rg_0a1b2c3d ts=6177770523, req=rg_0a1b2c3e ts=6177771600 — p99 jumped from ~140ms to ~1.2s for small generation calls (<= 200 tokens)
eng-infra: rolling driver + firmware was deployed to eu-west-2 last night at 6177769000 (driver 535.x, GPU FW 2.4.1). we also landed a kernel backport for blk-mq changes.
oncall: I'm looking at node metrics now. several nodes show GPU power dropping intermittently and host io wait spikes. top line: high iowait coincident with GPU clocks dropping.
eng-ml: could be thermal triggers on the new FW, or a KV cache eviction pattern causing host IO for KV persistence. Any dmesg or nvidia-smi anomalies?
support-ingress: attaching snippets:

```
[6177771601] dmesg: nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, admin q not responding
[6177771605] nvidia-smi: GPU 2 PERF: clocks throttled due to power
[6177771610] iostat -x 1 3: avg await 35ms -> spikes to 250ms
```

eng-infra: that nvme timeout stands out. storage tail latency + device resets can cascade into our RPCs that serve KV cache and model weights. looks like host IO starvation during bursts.
oncall: repro checklist: 1) fire 200rps tiny completions against eu-west-2 hosted endpoint with model redwood-small 2) observe p95/p99 for token gen 3) monitor /proc/diskstats, dmesg, nvidia-smi.
eng-runtime: repro ran on a canary VM: p95 went from 120ms -> 480ms after ~90s of sustained load, p99 spikes to 1.1s. correlates with nvme queue depth jumping to 128 and then transient device reset.
eng-ml: hypothesis: driver 535 introduced different DMA path interactions with the kernel blk layer; combined with new FW power management it triggers IO stalls under certain IO patterns (KV cache writes).
eng-infra: immediate mitigation options:
- route affected traffic to eu-west-3 (already healthy)
- increase node-level cgroup blkio.weight for inference pods to prioritize NVMe
- roll back driver/firmware (needs coord with cloud provider)
- enable local model-prefetching to avoid runtime writes

oncall: I started failover routing to eu-west-3 for the top 10% of Globex traffic. DNS and routing change applied :white_check_mark:
cust-success: letting Globex know we've routed most traffic away from eu-west-2 and we're investigating. their SLA team asked for ETA on full mitigation.
eng-runtime: quick config that helped in canary: set RUNTIME_ENV_VAR=KV_WRITE_SYNC=false and bump cache batch size to reduce write frequency. p99 dropped ~40% in canary but not ideal long term.
eng-infra: scheduling a driver rollback window with infra ops at 6177778000. plan: roll back to driver 533.x and FW 2.3.8 on a small subset first, validate, then full rollback.
eng-ml: also queueing an evaluation to see if we can change cache persistence frequency safely for all customers.
support-ingress: thanks — I'll keep the customer updated with the rollback window and the temporary routing. attaching logs and sample traces in the incident ticket.
eng-runtime: follow-up action items: 1) bisect kernel blk patches vs driver interactions 2) add guardrails to route on host iowait 3) postmortem once rollback validated
oncall: monitoring alert created: HOST_IO_WAIT_HIGH -> trigger auto-failover. alert ID: af-6177774012
deploy-bot: rollout event: eu-west-2 traffic policy changed at 6177774280 by oncall (failover to eu-west-3).
